newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks close higher in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks close higher in lackluster trade.

text.p: Brazil stocks ended slightly higher in weak trade Friday as investors ignored a drop on Wall Street and remained upbeat on next week's government-planned selloff of state miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce, brokers said.
"The day was very slow. There was no news that affected the market," said John Carioba of Indusval brokerage.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa .BVSP index of 49 most-traded shares closed up 0.23 percent at 9,732 points in sluggish trade of 356.8 million reais ($337 million).
Brokers said the bolsa, trading in a narrow range through the session, ignored a drop in the New York Stock Exchange and remained upbeat despite a lack of local market-moving news.
Many investors stayed on the sidelines but those who took part in the session were upbeat ahead of CVRD's privatization, originally set next Tuesday.
"Everybody's still waiting to see what happens but 70 to 80 percent of the market feels it will go ahead," one broker said.
But minutes after he made the comment, officials announced that a Sao Paulo judge late Friday had granted an injunction suspending the auction.
Stock prices were not affected by the ruling because news of the injunction came after the bolsa closed for the weekend.
Despite the optimism during the session, CVRD's preferred share remained stable at 27.00 reais while its common voter dropped 2.03 percent at 28.90 reais.
The day's rise was led by bellwether Telebras, whose preferred share ended up 0.46 percent at 120.25 reais while its voting common declined 0.7 percent to end at 113.60 reais.
Brazilian power stocks bucked the rising trend, sliding back some on the session to leave the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index off 0.3 percent at 2,669 points.
Despite the decline, blue chip Eletrobras' preferred rose 0.81 percent to end at 499.00 reais while the Minas Gerais state-owned Cemig rose 0.21 percent to close at 47.10 reais.
